reader.requirement: At --std 85 the library text named by text-name-1 replaces the whole COPY statement from the word COPY through its separator period inclusive, wherever the statement stands (inside a statement, a data description entry, a conditional sentence), so the COPY's period never survives into the resultant text.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the 2002 literal text-name/library-name and SUPPRESS phrase below 2002 (COBOL0900); the splice itself is unchanged
edition.Has(2002): a COPY inside library text is refused at 85 by the CopyNestedLibraryText2002 row (GR12); the splice of the found text is the same code
CopyUnqualifiedTextName2002: SR1 qualification refusal below 2002; no effect on the replacement
edition.ReplacedTextIsLaidOutInFixedForm (REPLACING layout only; not reached without REPLACING)

reader.edition-search: grep dialectLevel|edition.|EditionInfo|ConstructRegistry in CopyProcessor.cs; ExpandCopiesOneLevel and the statement-end scan (ParseCopyStatement/StatementCursor.ExpectSeparatorPeriod) consult no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the replacement of COPY through its period is the same code at 85 and 2023; only phrase gates (literal names, SUPPRESS, nested COPY, unqualified text-name) differ

reader.notes: ExpandCopiesOneLevel appends the text before the COPY keyword, splices the resolved library text between framing newlines, and resumes at afterCopy, the position ParseCopyStatement returns just past the separator period, so COPY through its period is replaced. A period inside pseudo-text does not end the statement (StatementCursor).

' then text after the COPY period on the same line ('FP.
